title: Face with Spiral Eyes Emoji 😵‍💫 Meaning: Dizzy, Overwhelmed
description: The face with spiral eyes emoji 😵‍💫 has swirling eyes and a wobbly mouth: dizzy, confused, overstimulated or mesmerized. See how it's used for brain fog.
summary: The 😵‍💫 face with spiral eyes means the sender's head is spinning. It describes physical dizziness and, more often, mental overload: too much information, a confusing explanation, a chaotic week. It can also mean hypnotized or dazzled by something, including a person the sender finds captivating.
meaning: Spiral eyes are how cartoons draw a character who has been spun around, hit on the head or hypnotized. 😵‍💫 brings that to the keyboard. Its plainest use is for vertigo and its relatives: motion sickness, a head rush, the after-effects of a roller coaster or a virtual reality headset.

The emoji found its real audience as a symbol of mental overload. It fits the feeling of having forty tabs open, of reading the same paragraph four times, of a group chat that produced two hundred messages while you were in a meeting. People with anxiety, attention difficulties or sensory overload use it to describe being overstimulated, because it shows a mind that cannot settle rather than one that has shut down.

Confusion is a close cousin. When instructions make no sense, a schedule keeps changing or a story has too many twists, 😵‍💫 says I am lost and slightly dazed by the attempt to follow. It is more helpless than the thinking face and less annoyed than the raised eyebrow, so it rarely offends the person who caused the confusion.

A lighter use is being entranced. Fans post it under a mesmerizing performance, an optical illusion or a pattern that is satisfying to watch, and people use it for a crush who has them under a spell. The swirls suggest hypnosis, so the emoji can mean I cannot look away as easily as I cannot think.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: It often answers how was your day when the day was chaos. It also follows a long or complicated message as an honest sign that the reader needs it broken down. Friends use it for hangovers and for the foggy feeling of waking from a nap at the wrong time.

contexts.label: At work and school
contexts.body: Deadlines, dense readings and software with too many menus bring it out. Sent to a teammate, it is a low-pressure request for help or a shared groan about complexity. It reads as overwhelmed but coping, which makes it more acceptable than faces that look sick or angry.

contexts.label: On TikTok and Instagram
contexts.body: Creators use it in captions about burnout, overstimulation and the mental load of running a household. It also labels trippy visual effects, fast transitions and illusions. In comments under a stunning person or performance, it means the viewer is dazzled.

contexts.label: In conversations about health
contexts.body: People managing migraines, vertigo, low blood pressure or medication side effects use it as quick shorthand for a dizzy spell. It communicates the symptom clearly to friends and family, though anyone feeling seriously unwell should spell out what is happening.

confusedWith.difference: 😵 has X eyes and means knocked out, stunned or finished. 😵‍💫 has swirls and means still conscious but reeling. Overwhelmed and spinning is the spiral; flattened and done is the Xs.
🥴 looks tipsy or lovestruck, with a lopsided smile, and often comments on something awkward. 😵‍💫 is about disorientation and overload and carries no hint of alcohol unless you add one.
💫 is a circling star, the symbol cartoons draw around a dazed head. Most people now use it as a decorative sparkle. 😵‍💫 combines that symbol with a face to show the actual feeling.

avoid: Do not use it to mock someone who is confused or struggling to keep up.
Avoid it as your full reply to detailed instructions from a boss; ask your question in words.
Remember that on outdated devices it can appear as two separate emojis, 😵 and 💫.
design: A yellow face whose eyes are replaced by dark spirals, with raised or uneven brows and a wavy, uncertain mouth. Technically it is a sequence that joins the crossed-out-eyes face with the dizzy symbol, and supported systems display the pair as one image. Designs are similar everywhere, differing mainly in how tight the spirals are.

faqs.q: What does 😵‍💫 mean from a guy or girl?
faqs.a: Usually that they are overwhelmed, confused or dizzy, with no hidden message. If they send it in response to your photo or a compliment, it means you have left them dazed, which is flirtatious. The topic of the conversation makes the difference obvious.

faqs.q: Why does 😵‍💫 show up as two emojis?
faqs.a: It is a combined sequence made of 😵 and 💫 linked by an invisible joiner character. Phones and apps that predate it do not know to merge them, so they display both pieces side by side. Updating the software resolves it.

It can describe the spinning room that comes with drinking, but that is not its main sense. The woozy face 🥴 is the usual tipsy emoji. 😵‍💫 more often means overstimulated, confused or lightheaded for sober reasons.

faqs.q: When was the spiral eyes emoji added?
faqs.a: It was introduced in Emoji 13.1, dated 2020, a small release that also brought the face exhaling, the face in clouds, the heart on fire and the mending heart. Phones received it in the software updates that followed.
